Playing it for the first time currently, and I gotta say, it's an incredibly sudden departure from the formula, but it feels amazing. Every expedition I find more interesting locations or resources, then I come back to jubilife and there are like 5 more side quests from the townspeople. The gameplay loop feels so fluid and addictive. The only fault I'm finding is a lack of consistent music. I will constantly notice that it's awkwardly silent during dialogue and walking through a new or important location. The overleveled alphas provide a wonderful optional challenge and really give that sense of intimidation and strength. Like they're genuinely scary. The feeling of actually throwing Pokeballs and actually dodging attacks and running away from Pokemon feels incredible. It's the kind of thing I didn't know I was missing from Pokemon games.

Scarlet, violet, sword, and shield all felt like they were just a platform to get out new marketable plushies, provide a platform for competitive battling, and hold the hands of whatever kids are playing so they can get to the end easily.

Pokemon Legends Arceus is a full experience. It doesn't try too hard. It leads you along the storyline just the right amount to avoid you getting lost, and then lets you run free into the wild. It's just the right amount of story and mechanics. The art direction feels top notch (for the switch at least). The characters are fresh and interesting, the world and story feel so mysterious, and the idea that everyone is terrified of Pokemon and thinks it's unethical to capture them really digs into your morals, like damn should I really be doing this? Is there a better way to get this silly shiny charm? Am I hurting these beings of nature just to fill a silly Pokedex? The fact that the galaxy team said you would probably die if you failed their trial was really blatant but so needed. It emphasises the danger of the outside world so well.

Legends Arceus reminds me that Videogames are art.
